subject: Supervised analysis on where tumour and matched normal are on seperate images.

messages.author: a647c82c283f7bff
messages.subject: Supervised analysis on where tumour and matched normal are on seperate images.
parts:
Hi team,

Have a question about the supervised analysis example, we have a similar scenario however the tumour and normal samples are on separate .imzML files. So when combining them and using the cvApply function each sample will only have one of the two response variables (i.e. all the pixels are either tumour or normal) which I would assume is problematic (and results with an error below when the summary() function is applied to the object). Is this a correct assumption? If so is there an alternative without having to try and re-export imzML files containing both tumour/normal one the one image?

As always, thanking you in advance!

-Dmitri

messages.author: 6033d3c0e7d242fa
messages.subject: Supervised analysis on where tumour and matched normal are on seperate images.
parts:
The default is to use separate runs as the CV folds, but this may not make sense for every dataset. Create a pixelData variable that defines the folds as you like (a factor or character vector with different levels for each fold, with length equal to the total number of spectra, where the elements define which fold each spectrum belongs to), and provide this as the argument to the .fold argument in cvApply.

(I’m on mobile right now and can’t give a more detailed example. Hopefully this helps.)

-Kylie
